prompt: What happened at the very beginning of the universe?
completion: Genesis 1:1 tells us: "In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth." This verse establishes that the universe had a definite starting point and that God Himself is the sovereign Creator who brought everything into existence by His word.

prompt: What does it mean that humans are made in the image of God?
completion: Genesis 1:26-27 says that God created humanity in His own image, male and female. Being made in God's image gives every human being inherent dignity, worth, and the capacity for relationship, creativity, and moral responsibility. It is one of the most foundational truths about human identity.

prompt: Why did God create marriage?
completion: Genesis 2:18 and 2:24 show that God said it was "not good" for man to be alone. He created woman and established marriage so that a man and woman would become "one flesh." Marriage was designed for companionship, unity, and to reflect God's relational nature.

prompt: What was work originally meant to be like before sin?
completion: Genesis 2:15 says God placed Adam in the garden "to work it and keep it." Work was originally a good and meaningful calling from God — not a curse. It only became painful and frustrating after sin entered the world (Genesis 3:17-19).

prompt: Why is there evil and suffering in the world?
completion: Genesis 3 explains that sin entered the world through human disobedience. Adam and Eve chose to doubt God and go their own way, which brought brokenness, shame, pain, and death into creation. All human suffering ultimately traces back to this event.

prompt: Is there any hope after humanity fell into sin?
completion: Genesis 3:15 gives the first promise of hope. God tells the serpent that one day an offspring of the woman would crush his head. This is the first glimpse of the gospel — pointing forward to Jesus, who would ultimately defeat sin and evil through His death and resurrection.

prompt: How did sin affect relationships between people?
completion: Genesis 3:16 shows that sin damaged the relationship between husband and wife, introducing conflict and power struggles. Genesis 4 shows it led to the first murder. Sin always damages relationships — with God and with other people.

prompt: What does the story of Cain and Abel teach us about sin?
completion: Genesis 4 shows how quickly sin progressed after the Fall. Cain's jealousy led to murder. It reveals that sin is serious, it affects our relationships, and it must be dealt with. God even warned Cain that "sin is crouching at the door" (Genesis 4:7).

prompt: Am I my brother's keeper?
completion: When God asked Cain where Abel was, Cain replied, "Am I my brother's keeper?" (Genesis 4:9). The answer is yes — we do have responsibility for one another. God holds us accountable for how we treat other people.

prompt: Why did God send the flood?
completion: Genesis 6:5 says the Lord saw that humanity's wickedness was great and "every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually." The flood was God's righteous judgment on widespread, persistent evil.

prompt: Can anyone live rightly when the world around them is very corrupt?
completion: Genesis 6:8-9 tells us that "Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord" and that he was "a righteous man, blameless in his generation." Even in a very dark time, it is possible to walk with God and live differently.

prompt: What does the rainbow represent?
completion: Genesis 9:13-16 explains that God set His bow in the clouds as a sign of the covenant. It represents God's promise never again to destroy the earth with a flood. The rainbow is a reminder of both God's judgment on sin and His mercy.

prompt: What does it look like to step out in faith when you don't know where you're going?
completion: Genesis 12:1-4 shows Abraham leaving his homeland because God told him to go. He obeyed without knowing the full destination. This is a powerful picture of walking by faith rather than by sight.

prompt: Can God really keep His promises when everything looks impossible?
completion: Genesis 18:14 records God asking Abraham and Sarah: "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" This comes right before the miraculous birth of Isaac in their old age. It shows that nothing is impossible for God.

prompt: What does real faith look like?
completion: Genesis 15:6 says: "And he believed the Lord, and he counted it to him as righteousness." Abraham trusted God's promise even when it seemed impossible. True faith is trusting God and His word, not our circumstances.

prompt: How should we respond when God asks us to do something very difficult?
completion: Genesis 22 shows Abraham willing to sacrifice Isaac when God asked him to. This story demonstrates radical trust and obedience, even when God's command doesn't make sense from a human perspective.

prompt: Why do bad things happen to good people?
completion: Joseph was betrayed by his brothers, sold into slavery, and falsely imprisoned. Yet Genesis 50:20 records him saying: "You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good." God can redeem even the most painful parts of our story.

prompt: What does it look like to forgive someone who deeply hurt you?
completion: After years of suffering because of his brothers, Joseph chose to forgive them and provide for them (Genesis 50:19-21). He didn't minimize what they did, but he refused to let bitterness control him.

prompt: How can we maintain integrity when life is unfair?
completion: Joseph maintained his integrity even when he was betrayed and thrown into prison. Genesis 39 repeatedly says "the Lord was with Joseph." He chose to honor God even when it cost him greatly.

prompt: Can God use our suffering for good?
completion: Joseph's suffering positioned him to save many lives during the famine, including his own family. Genesis 45:5-8 and 50:20 show that God can take what was meant for evil and use it for good.

prompt: What does it mean to walk by faith and not by sight?
completion: Abraham left his home not knowing where he was going (Genesis 12). He believed God's promises even when they seemed impossible. Walking by faith means trusting God's word and character more than what we can currently see or understand.

prompt: How should we respond when God's promises seem delayed?
completion: Abraham and Sarah waited 25 years for Isaac. During that time they struggled with doubt and even tried to fulfill God's promise their own way (Genesis 16). God's timing is often different from ours, but He is always faithful.

prompt: How can we trust God when life feels out of control?
completion: Joseph's life was full of events he didn't choose — betrayal, slavery, and prison. Yet he continued to trust that God was with him and working through his circumstances (Genesis 39:2-3, 21). Trusting God doesn't mean we understand everything.

prompt: What does it look like to maintain hope in difficult seasons?
completion: Even in prison, Joseph continued to use his gifts and serve others (Genesis 40). He didn't know how his story would end, but he kept trusting God. Hope in God allows us to keep moving forward even when we can't see the full picture.

prompt: What kind of spiritual legacy are we leaving for the next generation?
completion: Genesis shows both positive and negative generational patterns. Jacob passed on both faith and dysfunction. Joseph passed on forgiveness and trust in God. Our choices today have a real impact on those who come after us.

prompt: How important is it to speak blessing over our children and family?
completion: Before he died, Jacob gathered his sons and spoke specific blessings over each of them (Genesis 49). Speaking blessing and passing on spiritual truth is one of the most important things we can do for the next generation.

prompt: What does Genesis teach us about God's character?
completion: Genesis reveals God as Creator, Sovereign Ruler, Promise Keeper, Judge of sin, and Redeemer. He is both holy and merciful. He judges evil but also provides a way of salvation (seen clearly in the promise of Genesis 3:15).

prompt: Does God still pursue relationship with us even after we fail?
completion: After Adam and Eve sinned, God came looking for them (Genesis 3:8-9). After Jacob deceived others, God still met him and transformed him. God is remarkably patient and continues to pursue relationship with flawed people.

prompt: How should we respond when others treat us unfairly?
completion: Joseph was treated very unfairly multiple times. Instead of becoming bitter, he trusted God and continued to serve faithfully. His story shows that we can choose to respond with integrity even when others wrong us.

prompt: What does true success look like?
completion: By worldly standards, Joseph became very successful (second in command of Egypt). But his real success was his character, his forgiveness, and his trust in God through every season. True success is faithfulness to God, not status or wealth.

prompt: What does it mean to live with integrity when it costs you something?
completion: Joseph refused Potiphar's wife even though it cost him his position and freedom (Genesis 39). He chose to honor God rather than take the easy way out. Integrity often has a cost, but it is always worth it.

prompt: How should we view power and position?
completion: When Joseph rose to power, he used it to save lives rather than to get revenge. True godly leadership uses influence to serve and bless others, not to control or harm them.

prompt: What does reconciliation really require?
completion: Joseph didn't just forgive his brothers in his heart — he wept with them, reassured them, and provided for them (Genesis 45 and 50). Real reconciliation involves both forgiveness and a willingness to restore relationship where possible.

prompt: How can we keep our hearts soft toward God through difficult seasons?
completion: Joseph continued to trust God and use his gifts even in prison. He didn't become bitter. Keeping our hearts soft requires choosing to trust God's character even when we don't understand what He's doing.

prompt: What does it look like to finish well?
completion: Joseph finished well. He forgave his brothers, provided for his family, and made them promise to carry his bones back to Canaan (Genesis 50:24-25). Finishing well means staying faithful to God until the end.

prompt: What does Genesis teach us about God's sovereignty?
completion: Throughout Genesis we see that God is in control even when humans make bad choices. Joseph's story especially shows that God can take evil intentions and use them for good (Genesis 50:20). Nothing is outside of God's sovereign plan.

prompt: How does Genesis point to Jesus?
completion: Genesis 3:15 gives the first promise of a deliverer. Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac points to God sacrificing His own Son. Joseph's suffering and exaltation foreshadow Jesus. The whole book sets up the need for a Savior.

prompt: What does it mean to be blessed by God?
completion: God blessed Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph. Biblical blessing includes God's favor, provision, protection, and purpose. It is not just material wealth — it is God's presence and favor on a person's life.

prompt: How should we respond to God's calling on our life?
completion: Abraham responded with obedience (Genesis 12). Joseph responded with faithfulness in every situation. Responding well to God's calling means trusting Him and being faithful wherever He places us.

prompt: What does Genesis teach us about human nature?
completion: Genesis shows both the dignity of humanity (made in God's image) and our brokenness (the Fall and its consequences). We are capable of great good and great evil. We need God's grace and redemption.

prompt: Why is forgiveness so important?
completion: Joseph's ability to forgive his brothers allowed him to be free and to be used by God to save many people. Unforgiveness keeps us in bondage. Forgiveness is both a command and a pathway to freedom.

prompt: What does it look like to trust God with our family?
completion: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob all had to trust God with their families through many challenges. Trusting God with our family means praying for them, speaking truth to them, and believing God is at work even when we can't see it.

prompt: How can we live with purpose even when life feels meaningless?
completion: Joseph found purpose by serving others and trusting God even in prison. Our purpose isn't found in our circumstances but in our relationship with God and how we can bless others through whatever situation we're in.
